question: Two hours after undergoing allogeneic kidney transplantation for polycystic kidney disease, a 14-year-old girl has lower abdominal pain. Examination shows tenderness to palpation in the area the donor kidney was placed. Ultrasound of the donor kidney shows diffuse tissue edema. Serum creatinine begins to increase and dialysis is initiated. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

options.opa: T-lymphocyte activation by donor HLA peptides
options.opc: Preformed antibodies against class I HLA molecules
options.opd: Irreversible intimal fibrosis and obstruction of vessels
options.ope: Immune complex deposition in donor tissue

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Allogeneic kidney transplantation" -> "Lower abdominal pain post-transplantation" -> "Tenderness to palpation over donor kidney area" -> "Diffuse tissue edema on ultrasound of donor kidney" -> "Increasing serum creatinine" -> "Initiation of dialysis" -> "Acute rejection reaction" -> "T-lymphocyte activation by donor HLA peptides" -> 85%

analysis: The most likely cause of the patient's symptoms is acute rejection of the donor kidney, which is characterized by T-lymphocyte activation by donor HLA peptides leading to tissue edema, increased serum creatinine, and the need for dialysis.
